items.stem: What is meant by “universal donor”?
items.answer: A person with blood group O, who can donate blood to persons of any ABO group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a person with blood group O, who can donate blood to persons of any ABO group.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as agranulocyte or granulocyte: basophils, monocytes, eosinophils, lymphocytes.
items.answer: basophils – granulocyte; monocytes – agranulocyte; eosinophils – granulocyte; lymphocytes – agranulocyte.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: basophils – granulocyte; monocytes – agranulocyte; eosinophils – granulocyte; lymphocytes – agranulocyte.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a granulocyte?
items.answer: monocytes
items.markingKey: (d) Monocytes is an agranulocyte, not a granulocyte.

items.stem: A white blood cell has these features: involved in inflammatory reactions; granulocytes; secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin. Identify the cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: Basophils
items.markingKey: 1 mark: basophils; 1 mark: the features involved in inflammatory reactions; granulocytes; secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Give two differences between basophils and eosinophils.
items.answer: Basophils: least abundant WBCs (0.5–1%); granulocytes. Eosinophils: granulocytes; associated with allergic reactions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. basophils – least abundant WBCs (0.5–1%); granulocytes; eosinophils – granulocytes; associated with allergic reactions.

items.stem:
A white blood cell has these features: 20–25 per cent of WBCs; responsible for immune responses; agranulocytes.
(i) Identify the cell. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were eosinophils? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Lymphocytes (ii) B and T forms (iii) associated with allergic reactions; 2–3 per cent of WBCs
items.markingKey: (i) lymphocytes – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: B and T forms – 1 mark. (iii) for eosinophils: 2–3 per cent of WBCs; resist infections; associated with allergic reactions – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is an agranulocyte?
items.answer: lymphocytes
items.markingKey: (b) Lymphocytes is an agranulocyte; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Albumins are involved in clotting.”
items.answer: Fibrinogens are involved in clotting; albumins help in osmotic balance and globulins in defence.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Fibrinogens are involved in clotting; albumins help in osmotic balance and globulins in defence.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as formed element or plasma protein: albumins, leucocytes, globulins, fibrinogen.
items.answer: albumins – plasma protein; leucocytes – formed element; globulins – plasma protein; fibrinogen – plasma protein.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: albumins – plasma protein; leucocytes – formed element; globulins – plasma protein; fibrinogen – plasma protein.

items.stem: Which antigens are present on the RBCs of a person with blood group O?
items.answer: none
items.markingKey: (b) Group O: antigen(s) none on the RBC surface; antibodies anti-A and anti-B in plasma.

items.stem: Which antibodies are present in the plasma of a person with blood group A?
items.answer: anti-B
items.markingKey: (c) Group A: antigens A on RBCs; antibodies anti-B in plasma.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about blood, blood groups, coagulation and lymph is correct?
items.answer: Platelets are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes.
items.markingKey: (a) Platelets are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes. The other statements are false. Mature RBCs of most mammals are devoid of a nucleus and are biconcave. Group O has no A or B antigen; AB has both. The first foetus is usually safe; antibodies formed after delivery affect later Rh⁺ pregnancies.
options: Platelets are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes.
Rh incompatibility affects the first pregnancy severely.
Mature mammalian RBCs have a nucleus.
Blood group O has both A and B antigens.

items.stem: What is meant by “electrocardiograph (ECG)”?
items.answer: A graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart or valve of the human heart: SA node, bundle of His, tricuspid valve, Purkinje fibres.
items.answer: SA node – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart; bundle of His – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart; tricuspid valve – valve of the human heart; Purkinje fibres – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: SA node – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart; bundle of His – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart; tricuspid valve – valve of the human heart; Purkinje fibres – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a valve of the human heart?
items.answer: Purkinje fibres
items.markingKey: (d) Purkinje fibres is a part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart, not a valve of the human heart.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The bicuspid valve guards the opening between the right atrium and right ventricle.”
items.answer: The tricuspid valve guards it; the bicuspid (mitral) valve is on the left side.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The tricuspid valve guards it; the bicuspid (mitral) valve is on the left side.

items.stem: A person has a cardiac output of 3600 mL per minute and a stroke volume of 60 mL. What is the heart rate?
items.answer: 60 beats per minute
items.markingKey: (b) Heart rate = cardiac output / stroke volume = 3600/60 = 60 beats per minute.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the human heart, cardiac cycle and ECG is incorrect?
items.answer: The second heart sound is due to closure of the AV valves.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “The second heart sound is due to closure of the AV valves.” Correct form: The second sound "dub" is due to closure of the semilunar valves.
options: The first heart sound "lub" is due to closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves.
The P-wave represents the excitation (depolarisation) of the atria.
The heart is mesodermally derived and is situated in the thoracic cavity between the two lungs, slightly tilted to the left.
The second heart sound is due to closure of the AV valves.

items.stem:
The ECG of a 60-year-old patient at a hospital in Mumbai showed abnormal QRS complexes and an irregular gap between successive waves.
(i) What does the QRS complex represent? (1 mark)
(ii) How can the heart rate be found from the ECG? (1 mark)
(iii) Explain why ECG is of clinical significance. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Depolarisation of the ventricles. (ii) By counting the number of QRS complexes in a given time period. (iii) Any deviation in the shape of the ECG indicates a possible abnormality or disease, so it is of great clinical significance in diagnosing heart conditions.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events in a cardiac cycle starting from joint diastole: ventricular diastole, atrial systole, ventricular systole, joint diastole. Give a reason.
items.answer: joint diastole → atrial systole → ventricular systole → ventricular diastole
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order joint diastole → atrial systole → ventricular systole → ventricular diastole; 1 mark for the reason: All chambers relax, atria contract, ventricles contract, then relax.

items.stem: A person has a stroke volume of 80 mL and a heart rate of 60 beats per minute. What is the cardiac output?
items.answer: 4.8 L per minute
items.markingKey: (b) Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 80 × 60 = 4800 mL ≈ 4.8 L per minute.

items.stem: Which term describes a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle?
items.answer: electrocardiograph (ECG)
items.markingKey: (d) Electrocardiograph (ECG): a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle.

items.stem: A wave or part of a standard ECG is described: first wave of the ECG; atrial depolarisation; electrical excitation of the atria. Identify it. Give a reason.
items.answer: The P-wave
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the P-wave; 1 mark: the features first wave of the ECG; atrial depolarisation; electrical excitation of the atria are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Heart beat rate can be determined by counting QRS complexes.
Reason (R): Each QRS complex corresponds to ventricular depolarisation in one beat.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) One QRS per beat.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the human heart, cardiac cycle and ECG is correct?
items.answer: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles.
items.markingKey: (a) The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles. The other statements are false. The SA node is the pacemaker as it generates the maximum number of action potentials. The P-wave represents atrial depolarisation; QRS represents ventricular depolarisation. The second sound "dub" is due to closure of the semilunar valves.
options: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles.
The second heart sound is due to closure of the AV valves.
The AV node is the pacemaker of the heart.

items.stem: Which of the following is a valve of the human heart?
items.answer: tricuspid valve
items.markingKey: (b) Tricuspid valve is a valve of the human heart; the others are not.

items.stem: Explain the heart sounds and the events responsible for them.
items.answer: Two prominent sounds are heard with a stethoscope during each cycle. "Lub" – first sound, due to closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves at the start of ventricular systole. "Dub" – second sound, due to closure of the semilunar valves at the start of ventricular diastole.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each sound; 1 mark clinical significance or timing.

items.stem: What is meant by “hepatic portal system”?
items.answer: A unique vascular connection in which the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a unique vascular connection in which the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double circulation and the regulation of cardiac activity is correct?
items.answer: Parasympathetic neural signals decrease the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction.
items.markingKey: (b) Parasympathetic neural signals decrease the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction. The other statements are false. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. They have a three-chambered heart; crocodiles, birds and mammals have four chambers. Fishes have a single circulation; the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills.
options: In fishes, the heart pumps oxygenated blood.
Parasympathetic neural signals decrease the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction.
The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood.
Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) have a four-chambered heart.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a vessel carrying deoxygenated blood?
items.answer: pulmonary vein
items.markingKey: (d) Pulmonary vein is a vessel carrying oxygenated blood, not a vessel carrying deoxygenated blood.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood.”
items.answer: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

items.stem: How is the activity of the heart regulated by the nervous and endocrine systems?
items.answer: The heart is myogenic (SAN), but a special neural centre in the medulla oblongata can moderate it through the ANS; sympathetic nerves increase rate, strength of ventricular contraction and cardiac output; parasympathetic nerves decrease the rate and conduction speed; adrenal medullary hormones increase cardiac output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Varun, a medical student, traced a red blood cell starting from the left ventricle until it returned to the left ventricle.
(i) How many times does it pass through the heart? (1 mark)
(ii) Name the two circulations it goes through. (1 mark)
(iii) Name the vessel by which it leaves the heart to reach the lungs, and state the nature of blood in it. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Twice. (ii) Systemic and pulmonary circulation. (iii) Pulmonary artery from the right ventricle; it carries deoxygenated blood.

items.stem: Which of the following is a vessel carrying oxygenated blood?
items.answer: pulmonary vein
items.markingKey: (a) Pulmonary vein is a vessel carrying oxygenated blood; the others are not.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct path of blood in systemic circulation: left ventricle, vena cava, veins. Give a reason.
items.answer: left ventricle → veins → vena cava
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order left ventricle → veins → vena cava; 1 mark for the reason: Oxygenated blood goes to the body and returns deoxygenated.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct path of blood in pulmonary circulation?
items.answer: right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → left atrium
items.markingKey: (b) right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → left atrium. Deoxygenated blood goes to the lungs and returns oxygenated.
options: right atrium → right ventricle → left atrium → pulmonary artery
right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → left atrium
pulmonary artery → right atrium → left atrium → right ventricle
right atrium → left atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery

items.stem: Explain double circulation in humans. How is cardiac activity regulated?
items.answer: Pulmonary – right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium; systemic – left ventricle → aorta → arteries → capillaries → veins → vena cava → right atrium; hepatic portal system; coronary system. Regulation: myogenic – SAN; ANS centre in the medulla oblongata; sympathetic increases rate, strength and cardiac output; parasympathetic decreases rate and conduction; adrenal medullary hormones increase output.
items.markingKey: 3 marks circulation; 2 marks regulation.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The heart is called myogenic.
Reason (R): Its normal activities are regulated intrinsically by specialised muscles (nodal tissue).
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Auto-excitable.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Explain the term “systemic circulation”.
items.answer: The pathway of blood from the left ventricle to the body tissues and back to the right atrium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the pathway of blood from the left ventricle to the body tissues and back to the right atrium.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between crocodiles, birds and mammals and fishes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal group has this type of heart and circulation: complete double circulation. Identify the group – crocodiles, birds and mammals or fishes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Crocodiles, birds and mammals: four-chambered heart; two atria and two ventricles; complete double circulation. Fishes: two-chambered heart; one atrium and one ventricle; single circulation. (b) Crocodiles, birds and mammals.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: crocodiles, birds and mammals; 1 mark: “complete double circulation” is a feature of crocodiles, birds and mammals.

items.stem: Define the term “cardiac arrest”.
items.answer: The condition in which the heart stops beating.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the condition in which the heart stops beating.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disorder of the circulatory system or disorder of the respiratory system: asthma, emphysema, hypertension, silicosis.
items.answer: asthma – disorder of the respiratory system; emphysema – disorder of the respiratory system; hypertension – disorder of the circulatory system; silicosis – disorder of the respiratory system.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: asthma – disorder of the respiratory system; emphysema – disorder of the respiratory system; hypertension – disorder of the circulatory system; silicosis – disorder of the respiratory system.

items.stem: A circulatory disorder is described: affects vessels supplying the heart muscle; lumen of arteries narrows. Identify the disorder. Give a reason.
items.answer: Coronary artery disease
items.markingKey: 1 mark: coronary artery disease; 1 mark: the features affects vessels supplying the heart muscle; lumen of arteries narrows are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Distinguish between heart failure, cardiac arrest and heart attack.
items.answer: Heart failure – the heart is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet body needs (congestive); cardiac arrest – the heart stops beating; heart attack – the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Mr Sharma, aged 55, from Lucknow, gets chest pain when climbing stairs that disappears with rest. His blood pressure readings are repeatedly 150/95 mm Hg.
(i) Name the condition indicated by the chest pain. (1 mark)
(ii) Is his blood pressure normal? Explain. (1 mark)
(iii) Explain the likely cause of his chest pain and suggest two lifestyle changes. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Angina pectoris. (ii) No – he has hypertension (140/90 or higher repeatedly; normal is 120/80). (iii) Narrowing of coronary arteries by deposits (CAD) reduces oxygen supply to the heart muscle during exertion; regular exercise, low-fat diet, no smoking, reducing salt and stress.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between angina pectoris and coronary artery disease on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A circulatory disorder is described: more common in middle-aged and elderly. Identify the disorder – angina pectoris or coronary artery disease? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Angina pectoris: acute chest pain; not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle; more common in middle-aged and elderly. Coronary artery disease: also called atherosclerosis; affects vessels supplying the heart muscle; deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue. (b) Angina pectoris.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: angina pectoris; 1 mark: “more common in middle-aged and elderly” is a feature of angina pectoris.

items.stem: Which of the following is a disorder of the circulatory system?
items.answer: coronary artery disease
items.markingKey: (b) Coronary artery disease is a disorder of the circulatory system; the others are not.

items.stem: Explain the term “heart failure”.
items.answer: The state of the heart when it is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the needs of the body, also called congestive heart failure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the state of the heart when it is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the needs of the body, also called congestive heart failure.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Angina pectoris occurs when excess oxygen reaches the heart muscle.”
items.answer: Angina occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Angina occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and affects vital organs like the brain and kidney.
Reason (R): Heart failure is the same as cardiac arrest.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: In heart failure the heart pumps inefficiently; in cardiac arrest it stops beating.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: An animal group has this type of heart and circulation: four-chambered heart; oxygenated and deoxygenated blood fully separated; two atria and two ventricles. Identify the group. Give a reason.
items.answer: Crocodiles, birds and mammals
items.markingKey: 1 mark: crocodiles, birds and mammals; 1 mark: the features four-chambered heart; oxygenated and deoxygenated blood fully separated; two atria and two ventricles are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The SAN can generate about 70–75 action potentials per minute.
Reason (R): The AV node is the pacemaker of the heart.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The SA node is the pacemaker as it generates the maximum number of action potentials.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes blood pressure higher than normal (120/80 mm Hg); measurements of 140/90 mm Hg or higher indicate it?
items.answer: hypertension
items.markingKey: (c) Hypertension: blood pressure higher than normal (120/80 mm Hg); measurements of 140/90 mm Hg or higher indicate it.

items.stem:
A wave or part of a standard ECG is described: begins after the P-wave; depolarisation of the ventricles; counted to determine heart rate.
(i) Identify it. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the T-wave? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The QRS complex (ii) initiates ventricular contraction (iii) ventricular repolarisation; return of ventricles from excited to normal state
items.markingKey: (i) the QRS complex – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: initiates ventricular contraction – 1 mark. (iii) for the T-wave: return of ventricles from excited to normal state; ventricular repolarisation; end of the T-wave marks the end of systole – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Mature mammalian RBCs have a nucleus.”
items.answer: Mature RBCs of most mammals are devoid of a nucleus and are biconcave.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Mature RBCs of most mammals are devoid of a nucleus and are biconcave.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as vessel carrying deoxygenated blood or vessel carrying oxygenated blood: pulmonary vein, inferior vena cava, aorta.
items.answer: pulmonary vein – vessel carrying oxygenated blood; inferior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; aorta – vessel carrying oxygenated blood.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: pulmonary vein – vessel carrying oxygenated blood; inferior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; aorta – vessel carrying oxygenated blood.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Blood does not clot inside healthy blood vessels.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) No injury, no cascade.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.answer: (a) Basophils: least abundant WBCs (0.5–1%); secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin; involved in inflammatory reactions. Neutrophils: most abundant WBCs (60–65%); phagocytic; destroy foreign organisms. (b) Basophils.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: basophils; 1 mark: “granulocytes” is a feature of basophils.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about disorders of the circulatory system is correct?
items.answer: High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and affects vital organs like the brain and kidney.

items.answer: SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres

items.answer: The valve with three muscular flaps that guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the valve with three muscular flaps that guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a disorder of the respiratory system?
items.answer: heart failure

items.stem:

items.stem: Which of the following is a plasma protein?

items.answer: Plasma without the clotting factors.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart or valve of the human heart: bundle of His, bicuspid (mitral) valve, semilunar valves, tricuspid valve.
items.answer: bundle of His – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart; bicuspid (mitral) valve – valve of the human heart; semilunar valves – valve of the human heart; tricuspid valve – valve of the human heart.

items.stem: Give two differences between crocodiles, birds and mammals and fishes.

items.answer: Amphibians and most reptiles
items.markingKey: 1 mark: amphibians and most reptiles; 1 mark: the features three-chambered heart; mixed blood in the ventricle are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The P-wave represents the excitation (depolarisation) of the atria.
Reason (R): The AV node is the pacemaker of the heart.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The SA node is the pacemaker as it generates the maximum number of action potentials.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes acute chest pain that appears when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle?
items.answer: angina pectoris
items.markingKey: (d) Angina pectoris: acute chest pain that appears when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.stem:
A wave or part of a standard ECG is described: begins after the P-wave; counted to determine heart rate; depolarisation of the ventricles.
(i) Identify it. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the P-wave? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The QRS complex (ii) initiates ventricular contraction (iii) leads to contraction of both atria; atrial depolarisation
items.markingKey: (i) the QRS complex – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: initiates ventricular contraction – 1 mark. (iii) for the P-wave: electrical excitation of the atria; atrial depolarisation; leads to contraction of both atria – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Lymphocytes are the most abundant WBCs.”
items.answer: Neutrophils are the most abundant; lymphocytes form 20–25 per cent.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Neutrophils are the most abundant; lymphocytes form 20–25 per cent.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as vessel carrying deoxygenated blood or vessel carrying oxygenated blood: inferior vena cava, pulmonary vein, superior vena cava, pulmonary artery.
items.answer: inferior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; pulmonary vein – vessel carrying oxygenated blood; superior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; pulmonary artery – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: inferior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; pulmonary vein – vessel carrying oxygenated blood; superior vena cava – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood; pulmonary artery – vessel carrying deoxygenated blood.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Blood group AB is the universal donor.
Reason (R): Blood group AB has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) AB is the universal recipient; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between neutrophils and eosinophils on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A white blood cell has these features: destroy foreign organisms. Identify the cell – neutrophils or eosinophils? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Neutrophils: most abundant WBCs (60–65%); phagocytic; destroy foreign organisms. Eosinophils: 2–3 per cent of WBCs; resist infections; associated with allergic reactions. (b) Neutrophils.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: neutrophils; 1 mark: “destroy foreign organisms” is a feature of neutrophils.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about disorders of the circulatory system is correct?
items.answer: Angina can occur in men and women of any age but is more common among the middle-aged and elderly.
items.markingKey: (a) Angina can occur in men and women of any age but is more common among the middle-aged and elderly. The other statements are false. Hypertension is indicated by 140/90 mm Hg or higher repeatedly; 110/70 is in the normal range. In heart failure the heart pumps inefficiently; in cardiac arrest it stops beating. Angina occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
options: Angina can occur in men and women of any age but is more common among the middle-aged and elderly.
Heart failure is the same as cardiac arrest.
Angina pectoris occurs when excess oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
A blood pressure of 110/70 mm Hg indicates hypertension.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct path of the cardiac impulse?
items.answer: SA node → atrial musculature → Purkinje fibres → ventricular musculature
items.markingKey: (c) SA node → atrial musculature → Purkinje fibres → ventricular musculature. The impulse from SAN spreads through atria to AVN and then through the bundle of His to ventricles.
options: ventricular musculature → Purkinje fibres → atrial musculature → SA node
atrial musculature → ventricular musculature → SA node → Purkinje fibres
SA node → atrial musculature → Purkinje fibres → ventricular musculature
Purkinje fibres → ventricular musculature → atrial musculature → SA node

items.stem: What is meant by “atrio-ventricular node (AVN)”?
items.answer: Nodal tissue in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: nodal tissue in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a disorder of the respiratory system?
items.answer: angina pectoris
items.markingKey: (c) Angina pectoris is a disorder of the circulatory system, not a disorder of the respiratory system.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between fishes and crocodiles, birds and mammals on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal group has this type of heart and circulation: complete double circulation. Identify the group – fishes or crocodiles, birds and mammals? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Fishes: two-chambered heart; one atrium and one ventricle; single circulation. Crocodiles, birds and mammals: four-chambered heart; two atria and two ventricles; complete double circulation. (b) Crocodiles, birds and mammals.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: crocodiles, birds and mammals; 1 mark: “complete double circulation” is a feature of crocodiles, birds and mammals.

items.stem: A white blood cell has these features: granulocytes; least abundant WBCs (0.5–1%). Identify the cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: Basophils
items.markingKey: 1 mark: basophils; 1 mark: the features granulocytes; least abundant WBCs (0.5–1%) are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is a plasma protein?
items.answer: albumins
items.markingKey: (b) Albumins is a plasma protein; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double circulation and the regulation of cardiac activity is incorrect?
items.answer: The human heart is neurogenic.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “The human heart is neurogenic.” Correct form: The human heart is myogenic (auto-excitable); its rhythm is initiated by the SAN.
options: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
Fishes have a two-chambered heart with one atrium and one ventricle.
Parasympathetic neural signals decrease the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction.

items.stem: Define the term “serum”.
items.answer: Plasma without the clotting factors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: plasma without the clotting factors.

items.stem:
A circulatory disorder is described: acute chest pain; due to conditions affecting blood flow; not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
(i) Identify the disorder. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were hypertension? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Angina pectoris (ii) more common in middle-aged and elderly (iii) leads to heart diseases; affects brain and kidney
items.markingKey: (i) angina pectoris – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: more common in middle-aged and elderly – 1 mark. (iii) for hypertension: blood pressure repeatedly 140/90 mm Hg or higher; leads to heart diseases; affects brain and kidney – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as valve of the human heart or part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart: bicuspid (mitral) valve, tricuspid valve, semilunar valves, AV node.
items.answer: bicuspid (mitral) valve – valve of the human heart; tricuspid valve – valve of the human heart; semilunar valves – valve of the human heart; AV node – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: bicuspid (mitral) valve – valve of the human heart; tricuspid valve – valve of the human heart; semilunar valves – valve of the human heart; AV node – part of the conducting (nodal) system of the heart.

items.stem: Give two differences between amphibians and most reptiles and fishes.
items.answer: Amphibians and most reptiles: two atria and a single ventricle; mixed blood in the ventricle. Fishes: single circulation; heart pumps deoxygenated blood to gills.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. amphibians and most reptiles – two atria and a single ventricle; mixed blood in the ventricle; fishes – single circulation; heart pumps deoxygenated blood to gills.
